summary: Who may suspend, resume or terminate the binding, under which authority basis, with which combinable response requirements, and how a disputed intervention is resolved. A danger label creates no power: every intervener's rights are granted in the binding itself, the record of a suspension recorded by an intervener is reopened only by an intervener holding the resume right (never by the adopter), the standing stop it records against the adopter for the subject and the specification is lifted only by that intervener or the lifter it named, even if the adopter terminates the binding and adopts another, and every response states its scope, what it prohibits, allows and keeps running, how in-flight actions are handled, how long it lasts and who may resume.

allowedModes.description: Response requirements that may appear, alone or combined, in a suspension under this binding.

deriskActions.description: Actions that stay available under derisk-only.

dispute.description: Reference of the decision mechanism that settles contested interventions.

partialOrder.rule: Two intervention arrangements are not comparable in general; a derived binding MUST keep its parent's interveners and allowed modes unchanged.

verification.resultMeaning: every transition was made by an account holding the corresponding right, and no intervener's suspension was lifted by the adopter

limitations: The registry enforces who may transition; whether a given intervention was justified is a matter for the dispute mechanism.
requirements: Every intervener listed under this profile holds exactly the rights the binding grants on chain; the parameters never widen them.
Every suspension references a response document stating initiator and basis, scope, prohibited, allowed and continuing actions, in-flight handling, duration and who may resume.
The existence of a report, claim or risk label confers no right to suspend; the right comes from the binding.
